extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Econometrica; editors and referees of the journal
extracted.subtask_description: The journal's official editorial procedures and policies governing submission, review, revision, data and code availability, conflicts of interest, disclosures, experimental and AI-related requirements, and post-acceptance obligations for papers submitted to Econometrica.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process — formal submissions only; acknowledgement and manuscript number
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not pre-review papers; only formally submitted manuscripts are considered. Upon submission, an acknowledgment is sent and after membership confirmation and a compliance check a manuscript number (MS#) is assigned and should be cited in all correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission the review process begins once author membership and submission requirements are confirmed. Authors should cite their MS# in all correspondence. Authors experiencing unusual delays are encouraged to contact the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial triage and use of external referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Many submissions are sent to one or more referees, including Associate Editors, but some may be rejected after editorial evaluation without external review to save authors time and refereeing resources when a paper is clearly not a good fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts may be rejected, invited for revision, or accepted. Referee lists and decision-time statistics appear in Annual Reports. Unsolicited revisions of rejected papers will normally be rejected without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision offers and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An offer to revise is typically valid for 12 months from the decision date; extensions may be granted at the discretion of the handling Co-Editor but must be requested within that 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless specified otherwise by the Co-Editor, decisions are final. After acceptance, authors must return corrected page proofs within one year of receiving them for the article to proceed to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals policy (limited ground for appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are normally final; appeals are appropriate only when a clear factual error appears to have materially affected the decision (e.g., a referee misapplies a result whose conditions are not satisfied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disagreement with assessments of importance or relevance is not grounds for appeal. Disagreement with particular referee comments is not a basis for appeal because rejections generally reflect overall assessment rather than an isolated technical point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction grounds and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society reserves the right to retract a published paper in cases of (i) breach of the warranties stated in the copyright form; (ii) substantive errors; or (iii) evidence of scientific misconduct or other fraudulent actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A committee consisting of the Editors of the three Econometric Society journals and the Society’s President will evaluate and decide on proposed retractions. More information on procedures is available from COPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior and concurrent publication disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an author has submitted elsewhere work that overlaps with or includes parts of the current submission—before or during review at Econometrica—the author must disclose full details to the journal. This applies to all forms of publication other than working paper series or personal/institutional websites, including proceedings volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determining what constitutes prior publication may be complex and will be decided case by case. Submissions are evaluated relative to the published literature, including any material deemed previously published or under consideration elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use and authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use AI tools but remain responsible and accountable for all content of their work. AI software, such as chatbots or other large language models, may not be listed as an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author accountability includes careful review and verification of all AI-generated output, all analysis, interpretations, insights, and ideas, and safeguarding data privacy and intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity Check (plagiarism screening)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Econometric Society uses Similarity Check to screen submissions; submission to Econometrica implies consent to this electronic verification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect their submissions to be checked for overlap/plagiarism as part of initial processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and data/code availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals publish empirical, experimental, and simulation-based studies only when the underlying data and code are clearly documented and made available on a non-exclusive basis. Before acceptance, authors must provide raw data, code, and sufficient documentation to enable reproducibility checks on all empirical, experimental, and simulation results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If programs require long execution times or specialized hardware/software, authors should provide simplified versions and summary output files. Authors are expected to cooperate with the Data Editor in conducting reproducibility checks on selected parts of their materials without incurring a subscription cost. The extent of these checks must be recorded in the README file. Requests for exemptions or limitations must be clearly stated at initial submission; exemptions will not be considered later in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Code Availability Policy compliance (DCAS consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting to any Econometric Society journal, authors agree to the Society’s Data and Code Availability Policy, consistent with the Data and Code Availability Standard (DCAS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information on this policy and the Data Editor is provided by the Society (links on the journal website).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental papers — submission and pre-registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective January 1, 2026, all experimental paper submissions must include detailed experimental instructions or survey transcripts at the time of initial submission. Authors of studies that generate their own data must pre-register their studies in a recognized trial registry (e.g., AEA RCT Registry, AsPredicted, OSF Registries); pre-registration must specify the experimental protocol and the outcome variables of interest and be included as a separate file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy applies to laboratory, lab-in-the-field, and online experiments or surveys. While changes to data collection are not prohibited, any modifications must be clearly justified in the manuscript. Handling Co-Editors may request additional information during review, which could delay processing; authors are strongly encouraged to submit as complete a file as feasible. If accepted, additional materials to facilitate replication will be expected. During review supplementary materials are password-protected and accessible only to Co-Editors and reviewers for evaluation. If supplementary material is not in English, a translation must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental submissions — suggested procedural information
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested information to include for review: description of participant pool and recruitment; details on experimental technology, setting, format, and location; methods to assess participant understanding; matching procedures; payment details; number of participants per session and prior experience; session timing; any use of deception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should include these details either within the paper or an appendix; the handling Co-Editor may request additional specifics during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements (financial and other interests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submitted article must disclose its sources of financial support. Each author must disclose interested parties from whom they or a close relative/partner received financial support totaling at least US$10,000 in the past three years, and any paid or unpaid positions as officer, director, or board member of relevant organizations. If another party had the right to review the paper before circulation, that must be disclosed. For human-subjects research the corresponding author must disclose whether IRB approval was obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure statements for all published articles will be posted on the journal’s website. Authors complete disclosure forms through the online submission system; each coauthor receives a separate link. Disclosure information is available to referees. Failure to disclose relevant information may lead to reversal of acceptance or post-publication notices and referral to the Executive Committee. In cases of uncertainty, authors are encouraged to err on the side of full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility statements for multi-author papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective January 2026, accepted multi-author papers must include a responsibility statement indicating that authors accept responsibility for the content of the paper. The default statement is: 'All authors assume responsibility for all aspects of the paper.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams that assume specialized roles may provide a statement outlining respective responsibilities; the statement does not attribute specific contributions but indicates acceptance of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright transfer and open access options
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies agreement that copyright will be transferred to the Econometric Society if the article is accepted for publication. Authors may alternatively choose to publish open access by paying an article publication charge (APC) through the publisher (Wiley).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may post accepted versions on personal or institutional websites. Check institutional OA agreements with Wiley for eligibility; no payment is made to authors upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest rules for editors and handling of conflicted submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors, Co-Editors, Associate Editors, and the Data Editor are not permitted to handle papers authored by their current colleagues, thesis advisors, active co-authors, or individuals they advised (with timing restrictions). They also cannot handle papers by anyone they advised in a less central way if the submission occurs within two years of that person’s graduation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this policy, definitions are provided: a 'colleague' includes members of the same permanent department or certain members of other departments with collegial interaction; an 'active co-author' is a co-author on a paper in progress, under review/revision, or published less than two years ago; 'students advised in a less central way' include those for whom the editor wrote a letter of recommendation. Editors with conflicts will not have access to referee reports or names for papers covered by these conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and accessibility of editorial files
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports and cover letters remain in the editorial system; future Editors have access to them for 10 years and future Co-Editors for 6 years, limited to Editors and Co-Editors with no conflict of interest. All reports and cover letters are treated confidentially and referee identities and correspondence are never shared with authors, other referees, or Associate Editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy governs retention period and restricted internal access to editorial materials; authors and referees should expect confidentiality of referee identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing editorial files with other journals (on author request)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an author requests transfer of an editorial file to another Econometric Society journal, Econometrica may share (i) referee reports; (ii) the decision letter; and, with consent of individual referees, (iii) referee names and (iv) cover letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient journals are expected to honor Econometrica’s conflict-of-interest and confidentiality policies.
